chunks: # macOS hosted agents
Buildkite's macOS hosted agents are:
- [Buildkite agents](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent) hosted by Buildkite that run in a macOS environment.

- Configured as part of a _Buildkite hosted queue_, where the Buildkite hosted agent's machine type is macOS, has a particular [size](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#sizes) to efficiently manage jobs with varying requirements, and comes pre-installed with [software](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#macos-instance-software-support).
Buildkite macOS hosted agents are only available to Buildkite customers on [Pro or Enterprise](https://buildkite.com/pricing) plans.
- How to configure a macOS hosted agent in [Create a Buildkite hosted queue](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/queues/managing#create-a-buildkite-hosted-queue).
- How to use macOS hosted agents to [build iOS apps](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos/getting-started-with-ios).
- The [concurrency](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#concurrency) and [security](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#security) of macOS hosted agents.
- The [versioned queues](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#versioned-queues) pre-provisioned for new organizations, which pin a specific macOS version.

Buildkite offers a selection of macOS instance types (each based on a different size combination of virtual CPU power and memory capacity, known as an _instance shape_), allowing you to tailor your hosted agents' resources to the demands of your jobs.

| Instance shape | Size | vCPU | Memory | Disk space |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Instance shape | `MACOS_ARM64_M4_6X28` | Size | Medium | vCPU | 6 | Memory | 28 GB | Disk space | 182 GB |
| Instance shape | `MACOS_ARM64_M4_12X56` | Size | Large | vCPU | 12 | Memory | 56 GB | Disk space | 294 GB |
Also note the following about macOS hosted agent instances.
- Only [Apple silicon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_silicon) architectures are supported.
If you have specific needs for longer running hosted agents (over 4 hours), please contact Support at [support@buildkite.com](mailto:support@buildkite.com).
New Buildkite organizations are pre-provisioned with the following macOS hosted queues, in addition to `macos-medium` and `macos-large`:

| Queue | macOS version |
| --- | --- |
| Queue | `macos-14-medium` | macOS version | [Sonoma](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#macos-sonoma) |
| Queue | `macos-15-medium` | macOS version | [Sequoia](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#macos-sequoia) |
| Queue | `macos-26-medium` | macOS version | [Tahoe (26.6)](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#macos-tahoe-26-dot-6) |
| Queue | `macos-27-medium` | macOS version | [Golden Gate](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#macos-golden-gate) |

Each of these queues uses the `MACOS_ARM64_M4_6X28` (Medium) [instance shape](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#sizes) and pins its base image to the listed macOS version, rather than using the default image applied to queues without a version, such as `macos-medium`. GitHub Actions-style `macos-<version>` runner labels map to these queues. Route a job to the macOS version it expects by [targeting the matching queue](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/queues#targeting-a-queue-from-a-pipeline) in your pipeline.

New macOS hosted queues without an explicitly selected macOS or Xcode version default to macOS Tahoe (26.6) with Xcode 26.6. This includes queues you create and the `macos-medium` and `macos-large` queues created automatically for new Buildkite organizations. You can change this default at any time in the queue's **Base image** settings.
macOS hosted agents can operate concurrently when running your Buildkite pipeline jobs.

The number of macOS hosted agents (of a [Buildkite hosted queue](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/queues/managing#create-a-buildkite-hosted-queue)) that can process your pipeline jobs concurrently is calculated by your Buildkite plan's _maximum combined vCPU_ value divided by your [instance shape's](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#sizes) _vCPU_ value. See the [Buildkite pricing](https://buildkite.com/pricing/) page for details on the **Mac M4 Concurrency** that applies to your plan.

For example, if your Buildkite plan provides you with a maximum combined vCPU value is up to 24, and you've configured a Buildkite hosted queue with the `MACOS_ARM64_M4_6X28` (Medium) [instance shape](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#sizes), whose vCPU value is 6, then the number of concurrent hosted agents that can run jobs on this queue is 4 (that is, 24 / 6 = 4).
## [macOS instance software support](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos\#macos-instance-software-support)

All standard macOS [Golden Gate (27.0)](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#macos-golden-gate), [Tahoe (26.6)](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#macos-tahoe-26-dot-6), [Tahoe (26.5)](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#macos-tahoe-26-dot-5), [Tahoe (26.3.1)](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#macos-tahoe), [Sequoia](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#macos-sequoia), and [Sonoma](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#macos-sonoma) version instances have their own respective Xcode and runtime software versions available by default (listed below). Each macOS version also has its own set of [Homebrew packages](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#homebrew-packages) with specific versions optimized for that operating system. If you have specific requirements for software that is not listed here, please contact Buildkite Support at [support@buildkite.com](mailto:support@buildkite.com).

While you currently cannot provide custom base images for macOS hosted agents (as is possible using [agent images](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/linux#agent-images) for Linux hosted agents), you do have significant control over these virtual machines during job execution—including the ability to install software using Homebrew, use [git mirroring](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/cache-volumes#git-mirror-volumes) for performance, and use persistent [cache volumes](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/cache-volumes).

Older Xcode versions are removed from base images over time. If your queue has an Xcode version pinned that is no longer available, a warning is displayed on the queue list and queue settings pages: "Xcode {version} is no longer available for this macOS version. Your agents may fail to start until you update the base image of your queue." To resolve the warning, navigate to the queue's **Base image** settings and select an available Xcode version.

Three macOS Tahoe versions are available, each with a unique set of Xcode versions. [Tahoe (26.3.1)](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#macos-tahoe) includes older Xcode versions, because certain older Xcode versions are incompatible with newer Tahoe base images. [Tahoe (26.5)](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#macos-tahoe-26-dot-5) and [Tahoe (26.6)](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#macos-tahoe-26-dot-6) include newer Xcode 26.x versions.
### [Docker support](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos\#macos-instance-software-support-docker-support)

macOS hosted agents include the Docker CLI (through the `docker` and `docker-buildx` [Homebrew packages](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#homebrew-packages)), but do not include a running Docker daemon. Commands that require a Docker daemon, such as `docker build` or `docker run`, fail with an error like `Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock. Is the docker daemon running?` unless the job connects to a Docker daemon that you provide.

To build Docker images, run these jobs on [Linux hosted agents](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/linux), which support Docker image builds (including [remote Docker builders](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/linux/remote-docker-builders) on the Enterprise plan), or on [self-hosted agents](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted), where you control the Docker installation.

The versions for each of these packages varies by macOS version. See [Identifying Homebrew package versions](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#homebrew-packages-identifying-homebrew-package-versions) for instructions on how to identify each package's version.
To find the [Homebrew package](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted/macos#homebrew-packages) version used by your macOS hosted agent:

1. Select **Agents** in the global navigation > your [cluster](https://buildkite.com/docs/pipelines/security/clusters/manage) containing the [macOS Buildkite hosted agent queue](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/queues/managing) \> your macOS hosted agent.
2. On your macOS hosted agent's page, select **Base image** and scroll down to **Specifications** \> **Homebrew packages** to view these packages, along with their respective versions.

Homebrew package versions are periodically updated when macOS hosted agent images are refreshed. If your builds require explicit, repeatable versions, pin the versions you need as part of your pipeline rather than relying on the image defaults.

```
brew list --versions
brew info <formula>
brew info <formula>@<major>     # when the formula supports versioned installs
```

The shift from a [self-hosted](https://buildkite.com/docs/pipelines/architecture#self-hosted-hybrid-architecture) to a [Buildkite hosted](https://buildkite.com/docs/pipelines/architecture#buildkite-hosted-architecture) architecture for Buildkite agents, introduces the potential for new attack vectors and shared responsibility models, and hence, additional security considerations.

Note that for macOS hosted agents, virtualization is achieved through Apple's Virtualization framework on Apple Silicon, providing lightweight but secure virtual machine isolation. Learn more about [How Buildkite hosted agents work](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/buildkite-hosted#how-buildkite-hosted-agents-work).
